ov: Squirrel-sized New World monkeys in 22 species, many with moustache-like facial hair. They run and leap through tropical rainforest and open forest, and usually have twins, which the whole group helps to raise.
rg: From southern Central America to central South America: northwestern Colombia, the Amazon basin and the Guianas.
df: Omnivores: fruit and other plant parts, spiders, insects, small vertebrates and birds’ eggs.

cf.tip: Marmosets are close relatives in the same family; they gnaw holes in trees to feed on gum and sap.

fx: Groups can have up to 40 members, but usually have just three to nine.
In captivity, cotton-top tamarins have lived up to 23 years.
